chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ma'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a child is born, an animal is sacrificed for him, his head is shaved, and the weight of his hair in silver is given as charity. A leg with the thigh is presented to the midwife. A group of Muslims are invited to eat and supplicate for the boy, and he is named on the seventh day."

key_terms.الْوَرِكَ: The thigh (part of the sacrificed animal)
key_terms.عَقَّ: Sacrificing an animal (aqiqah) on behalf of a newborn

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and sunnahs for a newborn child in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the Sunnah of welcoming a newborn, emphasizing gratitude through the 'aqiqah' sacrifice and proportional charity (weight of hair in silver/gold) as acts of spiritual purification. It highlights the communal aspect of Islamic parenting by inviting guests to share in the joy and prayers, while also noting the practical care for the midwife, reflecting the holistic social and spiritual dimensions of family life in Shia jurisprudence.
